summary.headline: Carborundum Universal Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 21.2% YoY to INR 846 crores; consolidated PAT up 23.4% to INR 76 crores, with Electrominerals up 33%.
summary.overview: Standalone sales grew 21.2% YoY to INR 846 crores, broad-based across Electrominerals (+33%), Ceramics (+15.2%) and Abrasives (+14.7%), and were flat QoQ. Standalone PAT was INR 88 crores, up 14.3% on a like-to-like basis excluding a one-time INR 68 crore subsidiary dividend in Q1 FY26. Consolidated PAT of INR 76 crores was helped by a INR 25 crore gain on leasehold transfer at Sterling Abrasives, while Abrasives standalone margins were squeezed by an oil-linked and fuel cost push of about INR 16 crores. Management raised the consolidated Ceramics growth guidance to 23-25% and kept other segment guidance unchanged, while Foskor divestment and Awuko closure updates are now promised for Q2.

segments.name: Electrominerals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 282 crores, +33% YoY and +12.2% QoQ, mainly volume and export-led with very little price increase; PBIT rose to INR 39 crores from INR 7 crores. Exports rose to about 40% of segment sales from about 35% last year.

segments.name: Ceramics (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 274 crores, +15.2% YoY but -1.6% QoQ on refractories seasonality; PBIT INR 59 crores vs INR 62 crores YoY as IC gains were offset by fuel, alumina and unabsorbed costs in new semicon and aerospace/defence lines.

segments.name: Abrasives (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 328 crores, +14.7% YoY, volume-driven; PBIT INR 34 crores with margin falling to 10.4% from 13.1% YoY, due to about INR 16 crores cost push (resins, oil, fuel) and INR 8-9 crores volume drop QoQ.

segments.name: Rhodius (Germany, Abrasives)
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 15.6 million, +18% YoY and +1.1% QoQ (INR 172 crores, +33.9% YoY); loss after tax EUR 0.7 million vs EUR 1.6 million a year ago. FY27 guidance of about 5% growth and a small PAT loss is maintained.

segments.name: CUMI Awuko Abrasives (Germany, being wound up)
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 2.89 million, +11.1% YoY; loss after tax EUR 1.69 million vs EUR 0.9 million a year ago. Voluntary winding up is in progress and management aims to complete it in about a quarter.

segments.name: VAW Russia (Electrominerals)
segments.commentary: Sales RUB 1.58 billion, -14.1% YoY in roubles but INR 201 crores, +3.1% YoY in rupee terms; PAT RUB 52.1 million vs RUB 71.5 million a year ago. Business is domestic-focused.

segments.name: Foskor Zirconia (51% subsidiary, Electrominerals)
segments.commentary: Sales ZAR 107 million, -14.7% QoQ; deemed commercially unviable. Q1 consolidated PBIT absorbed a INR 17 crore loss; divestment or exit options are being explored, targeted for Q2.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated sales growth: FY27 guidance of about 4-4.5% reported, or 11-12% excluding Foskor and Awuko; management says it could reach about 15% on a comparable basis given the order book.
Consolidated Abrasives sales growth: guidance of 5.5-6% retained; 11-12% excluding Awuko (about INR 108 crores).
Consolidated Ceramics sales growth: raised to 23-25% from 15-15.5%; management expects the Ceramics margin to be at the higher end of the guidance.
Consolidated Electrominerals sales: guidance of a 6.5-7% decline retained (reported basis); 8-9% growth excluding Foskor, and management says this could be 9-10%.

Margins: Abrasives 9.5-10% and Electrominerals 9-9.5% retained, with Ceramics 20.5-21% maintained. Q1 consolidated Abrasives margin was about 2.5% excluding the Sterling gain, which management attributes to Awuko losses.
Capex of about INR 400 crores for FY27 retained. Rhodius guidance of about 5% growth with a small PAT loss is unchanged.
capex_capacity: Consolidated capex was INR 53 crores in Q1 FY27 against INR 64 crores a year earlier; the FY27 target of about INR 400 crores is unchanged, and management would not give project-wise splits.

FY27 capex covers expansion in advanced ceramics for power electronics (including substrates), metallized tubes, rings and brazed assemblies, brown-fused alumina expansion, an integrated furnace for thermal spray powders and a zirconia furnace.
Metallized substrate facility is being set up with one anchor customer and a technology tie-up; it should be commissioned in FY27, with revenue from FY28.

Semiconductor wafer fab equipment components: small in FY27, picking up in FY28, with a peak targeted for FY30. Aerospace and defence will improve in FY27 with the main ramp from FY28. Powder purity is moving from 5N to 6N.
Refractories capacity expansion is on track, per management.
demand_pricing: Standalone Abrasives growth was volume-driven with very small price increases; management sees early easing of Chinese import competition but says exchange rates and China's export-rebate changes make the trend unclear.
Ceramics: growth was seen across segments; Wear Ceramics returned to growth this quarter after several quarters, and Metallized Cylinders and Engineered Ceramics are growing mainly through exports.

Electrominerals: volume-led, with treated-product mix helping margins; little or no price increase. Export share is rising toward 40%, helped by European duties on Chinese imports, with US and Asia efforts under way.

Abrasives cost push: oil-linked inputs such as resins rose sharply in May and June, with oil reaching about $117 a barrel. Grains (80-85% of COGS) rose only 3-5%. The US-Iran conflict that began end-February 2026 drove the cost pressure.
Management said it will not pass on further price increases until the cost environment is clearer, and will decide one quarter at a time.
